messages:
maya: Heads up — several GPU batch workers in us-west-2 are failing LSF jobs after the new base-image rollout.
maya: Error is `libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory` when the container runtime starts the trainer.
sam: Which image tag got rolled? can you paste the node labels/host OS? :thinking:
maya: image: redwood/gpu-base:2025-05-13
maya: nodes affected: gpu-type=a100, k8s v1.27, kernel 6.1.x, about 12 nodes across two AZs
linus: We pushed a small baseimage bump this morning that included nvidia-container-toolkit 1.12.0 -> 1.13.0.
linus: Deploy bot also logged the canary: `deploy-bot: canary roll redwood/gpu-base:2025-05-13 -> success` at 2025-05-13T09:01:22Z
deploy-bot: canary roll redwood/gpu-base:2025-05-13 completed on canary nodes
carla: 1.13 changed how /var/lib/nvidia is bind-mounted by the toolkit in containerd setups. We saw similar in staging last month but patch fixed it by ensuring the runtime mounts host libs into container with `rshared` propagation.
maya: here's the containerd event log snippet from one failed pod:
maya: ```
containerd: start container failed: error mounting "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1" to "/run/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/moby/abc123/rootfs/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1": not a directory: unknown
``` 
sam: So mount propagation or hostPath semantics changed. Are these nodes using host-init or initContainers to copy libs?
linus: We used hostPath mounts originally, relying on `mountPropagation: Bidirectional` on the kubelet. The new toolkit seems to expect a different bind mode when containerd does the bind.
ryan: Ops-bot shows GPU node count drop and pods in CrashLoopBackOff — autoscaler started evicting TF jobs.
ops-bot: ALERT: 12 GPU nodes NotReady in cluster-us-west-2-gpu; 47 pods evicted. See: https://console.redwood/internal/incidents/INC-20250513-73
carla: Quick workaround: pin base image to previous tag and cordon/drain updated nodes to force redeploy to older image. Also we can set `mountPropagation: HostToContainer` + ensure host lib path exists as directory.
sam: Any chance we can patch containerd config to preserve rshared on /usr/lib mounts? That might be lower friction than full rollback.
linus: Possibly. But kernel+containerd behavior varies by distro. eu-west cluster still on old baseimage so not affected — region constraint buys us time.
maya: I'm going to roll back the image on the autoscaling groups for the affected pools. Will also open a ticket to coordinate a toolkit-specific fix.
maya: rollback plan: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) drain with `--ignore-daemonsets` 3) replace ASG launch template to gpu-base:2025-05-12 4) uncordon after nodes rejoin
sam: If you need help running drains I can run them in the 2 AZs.
ryan: Cost note: If we keep extra nodes up while rolling, nightly autoscaler will increase bills. Try to sequence so we don't double-provision for too long.
carla: Longer-term: add a preflight test in our canary pipeline that runs `ldd /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1` inside a minimal container to assert toolkit mount present.
linus: Also opening PR to pin toolkit to 1.12.x for the minor release train until we validate 1.13 across distros.
maya: 👍 starting rollback now. I'll update thread with progress.
maya: 10:07 — cordoned az1 nodes, draining az1
sam: 10:10 — helping on az2
maya: 10:23 — az1 nodes replaced and passing GPU health checks. restarting batch queue.
maya: 10:35 — az2 replaced, cluster stable. no more libcuda errors observed.
ryan: Great. Please add postmortem notes about region divergence and canary sample size. We need better telemetry on containerd mountprops during canary.
carla: Filed ticket INFRA-4523 with reproduce steps and logs. Assigned to eng-infra and runtime.
linus: Followup: we should test toolkit 1.13 on debian/ubuntu/centos variants before promoting.
maya: Thanks everyone. Closing thread once INFRA-4523 has RCA and mitigation plan. :thumbsup:
